hero.title: Comparing CNN architectures for fine-grained dog breed classification
hero.description: The thesis evaluates multiple transfer learning architectures based on fine-grained classification accuracy, computational efficiency, parameter count, and deployment latency.

objectives.title: Research Objectives
objectives.obj1Desc: Achieve top-1 and top-5 accuracy on fine-grained dog breed classification tasks.
objectives.obj2Desc: Minimize response time for real-time web application deployment using ONNX Runtime.
objectives.obj3Desc: Evaluate model weight size and memory footprint for edge-friendly deployment.
objectives.obj4Desc: Integrate Grad-CAM visual attention mapping to enhance user trust and model transparency.

models.title: Evaluated CNN Architectures
models.resnetDesc: Deep residual network utilizing skip connections to overcome vanishing gradients in fine-grained feature learning.
models.efficientnetDesc: Compound scaling architecture balancing depth, width, and image resolution for high parameter efficiency.
models.mobilenetDesc: Hardware-aware neural architecture search optimized for low latency mobile and web runtime execution.

matrix.title: Architecture Evaluation Matrix
matrix.subtitle: Comparative baseline benchmarks across transfer learning candidate models
matrix.academicNotice: Academic Integrity Notice: Final quantitative metrics will be populated upon completion of model fine-tuning and evaluation on test splits.

dataset.title: Stanford Dogs Dataset
dataset.description: The research baseline utilizes the Stanford Dogs Dataset, containing fine-grained category images collected for testing fine-grained visual categorization algorithms.
